seo.siteTitle: OrderOrange — приложение доставки еды: закажите онлайн в ресторанах
seo.siteBlurb: Приложение доставки еды. Заказывайте онлайн в ресторанах, кафе, магазинах и аптеках: гриль, бургеры, пицца, арабская, индийская и иранская кухня — с доставкой или самовывозом. Бесплатно для ресторанов, без комиссии. Заказывайте в чате или голосом с ИИ-помощником OrderOrange. OrderOrange — ещё и бесплатная POS-система для ресторана: касса, кухонный экран, QR-меню, склад и отчёты.

pos.h1: Free, open-source POS system for restaurants, cafés & shops — any country, any currency
pos.lede: OrderOrange is two things in one account. It is the till your staff use all day — orders, tables, payments, printed bills, stock, staff and reports — and it is the page your customers order from online. Nothing is typed twice, because both read the same menu.
pos.free: Free POS. No monthly fee, no setup fee, no commission.
pos.guide: See all 41 screens in the guide
pos.tillB: Open a table or a walk-in ticket, tap the dishes, take cash or card, print the bill. The till runs in any browser — the counter screen, a laptop, a tablet in your hand — and there is a layout built for each. The menu opens instantly because photos load only for the group you tap.
pos.tablesB: Draw your floor: rooms, table shapes, seats. Print a QR code for every table and guests order from their own phone straight onto that table's bill, and can message the counter from the same screen. You see every open table and what is on it.
pos.kdsB: A screen for the kitchen instead of a printer: new tickets arrive in columns, each one counting the minutes since it was sent, turning amber and then red when it runs late. Cooks tick off a line as it is plated and bump the ticket when it is done. Each station can show only its own items.
pos.menuB: Categories, options, photos and prices once. Every dish carries its name in fourteen languages, can be kept on the till but hidden from the website, and can appear only on the days and hours you choose. Search finds a dish however it is spelled.
pos.printingT: Prints to the printer you already own
pos.printingB: A small Windows program connects the till to any ESC/POS receipt printer, and product printers send each part of an order to the right station — drinks to the bar, grills to the kitchen. Every bill carries a code a guest can check for themselves.
pos.stockB: Raw materials, recipes and consumption: sell a dish and its ingredients come off the shelf. Reports show what a plate actually costs you and what is about to run out, so an order goes in before the shelf is empty.
pos.purchasingB: Scan goods in against a supplier, keep their invoices and what you still owe them, and print your own barcodes and shelf labels. Payments to suppliers sit in the same ledger as everything else.
pos.staffB: Give each person exactly the screens they need through a permission matrix — a waiter does not see your margins. Staff clock in and out with GPS, ask for leave, and the salary run reads the hours it produced.
pos.customersB: Keep your own customer list, send discount codes with real conditions (first order, amount spent, certain hours, certain days), run a short survey, read reviews, and take table bookings online.
pos.reportsB: Daily takings, sales by product, by customer and by hour, consumption, production capacity, salaries, attendance, delivered orders, bill history and survey results. Every report exports to Excel and prints on A4.
pos.invoicesB: Cancel or correct an invoice and the original is kept rather than overwritten, with who did it and why. Design the bill itself — logo, columns, footer — in the invoice designer.
pos.onlineT: Online ordering in the same account
pos.onlineB: The same menu becomes your shop page on orderorange.com, takes delivery and pickup orders, and tracks the rider to the door. An AI assistant lets a customer order by chatting or speaking.
pos.branchesB: Add a second business and switch between them from the top of the screen. Stock, staff and reports stay separate; you stay one person with one password.
pos.apiB: Tokens, GET and POST, documented with worked examples, so your accounting, CRM or ERP software can read orders and post products without anyone retyping them.
pos.priceBody: Opening an account is free and there is no commission on what you sell. The till, the kitchen display, the reports and your online page all work on the free plan.
pos.q1: Is OrderOrange really a POS system, or just a delivery app?
pos.a1: It is a full point of sale. Tables, tickets, payments, printed bills, kitchen display, stock, staff and reports are all part of it. Online ordering is one more thing the same account does, not a separate product.
pos.a2: Any computer, tablet or phone with a browser. For printed bills, a USB or network ESC/POS receipt printer and the free Windows program. A barcode scanner and a screen for the kitchen are optional.
pos.q3: Can I use it in Arabic?
pos.a3: Yes. The whole system is in fourteen languages including Arabic, Persian and Urdu, laid out right to left, with Arabic and Persian numerals where they belong.
pos.q4: How long does it take to start?
pos.a4: You create an account with a username and a password. The menu, the floor plan and the first reports can be ready the same day, and the guide walks through every screen with real pictures.
pos.a5: No. Cafés, bakeries, markets, pharmacies and shops run on the same till, using barcodes and shelf labels instead of table service.
pos.q6: Can it connect to my accounting software?
pos.a6: Yes. There is a documented REST API with tokens, so another system can read your orders and invoices or push products in.
pos.alsoBody: The same account puts your shop in front of everyone ordering food, with no commission taken from the order.
seo.posTitle: Free Open-Source POS for Restaurants, Cafés & Shops | OrderOrange
seo.posDesc: Free, open-source POS for restaurants, cafés and shops: till on any tablet, kitchen display, QR menu, online orders with 0% commission. No monthly fee, any currency, 14 languages. Code on GitHub.
kds.title: Kitchen display
kds.allClearSub: New tickets appear here the moment they are ordered.
partner.currencyHint: Shown on every screen of your portal and on what you print: the till, invoices, reports and the kitchen screen.
pos.globalB: Nothing here is tied to one country. Pick the symbol your prices wear — rials, dirhams, riyals, rupees, dollars, euros, or type your own — and set your own tax rate, opening hours and delivery areas. The portal and the customer app read in fourteen languages, right to left where they should, and receipts print in the language your kitchen reads. Prices are never converted: they stay exactly as you typed them.
pos.q7: Can I use it in my country?
pos.a7: Yes. Choose your currency symbol, your tax percentage, your opening hours and your delivery areas, and run the whole system in any of fourteen languages. A shop in Dubai, Riyadh, Istanbul, Delhi or London works exactly like any other — no country is built in.
pos.webmenuB: Your menu gets its own web address — orderorange.com and your shop's name — with photos, prices, options and a description of every dish, in fourteen languages. It is the same menu the till sells from, so it can never be out of date: change a price once and the website, the QR code at the table and the printed ticket all change together. No app to download, nothing to design, and no PDF anyone has to pinch to zoom. Put the link in your Instagram bio, send it on WhatsApp, or print it as the QR code on the table.
pos.q8: Do I get an online menu?
pos.a8: Yes, free with the account. Your shop gets a page at orderorange.com with your dishes, photos and prices in fourteen languages, and a QR code for each table that opens the same menu. It updates itself, because it reads the menu your till already uses. Guests can browse it, or order from it for delivery or pickup.

pos.freeTitle: A free POS system — and what “free” means here
pos.freeLede: Most point-of-sale software charges a monthly fee per terminal, a setup fee, and often a cut of every online order. OrderOrange charges none of those. Everything below comes with a free account, for as many users, tables and screens as you need.
pos.free1B: The till itself — tables, tickets, cash and card, printed bills — with no monthly fee and no per-terminal fee. Add a second counter or a tenth waiter without paying more.
pos.free2T: Free POS app for tablets and phones
pos.free2B: Open the till in the browser of any tablet or phone, or use the light tablet screen built for older Android tablets and iPads that no longer get updates. No app store, nothing to install.
pos.free3B: Turn any screen in the kitchen into a ticket board instead of buying a printer. Tickets arrive by themselves, count their minutes and turn red when they run late.
pos.free4T: Free QR menu and online menu
pos.free4B: Every table gets a QR code and every shop gets a page at orderorange.com with photos and prices in fourteen languages. Both read the same menu the till sells from, so nothing is ever out of date.
pos.free5B: Delivery and pickup orders from your own page go straight into the till. You keep the whole ticket — there is no commission on anything you sell.
pos.free6B: The Windows program that drives your ESC/POS receipt printer, the stock and recipe module, purchasing by barcode, staff attendance and every report — Excel export included — are all part of the free plan.
pos.free7B: A second café or a third kitchen is another business in the same login, with its own stock, staff and reports, at no extra cost.
pos.free8B: New screens and fixes arrive in the browser by themselves. There is no version to buy and no upgrade fee.

pos.cmp6b: Any browser, any ESC/POS printer, any barcode scanner
pos.whoTitle: Who runs on a free POS
pos.whoBody: Restaurants and grills, cafés and coffee shops, bakeries, shawarma and burger counters, juice bars, food trucks and cloud kitchens, small markets, pharmacies and shops — anyone who takes orders at a counter or a table and wants the numbers at the end of the day without paying a licence for them.
pos.whereTitle: Free POS anywhere: Dubai, Riyadh, Istanbul, Delhi, London…
pos.whereBody: Nothing in OrderOrange is tied to one country. Pick your currency symbol — rials, dirhams, riyals, dinars, pounds, lira, rupees, dollars, euros, or type your own — set your tax rate, opening hours and delivery areas, and run the whole system in any of fourteen languages. The same free POS works exactly the same in Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Riyadh, Jeddah, Doha, Kuwait, Manama, Cairo, Amman, Istanbul, Tehran, Karachi, Delhi, Mumbai, London, Paris, Berlin, Madrid, Lisbon, Moscow, Tokyo and Shanghai.
pos.q9: Is the POS really free, or is it a trial?
pos.a9: It is free, not a trial. The account does not expire, there is no card to enter, and the till, kitchen display, QR menu, online menu, stock and reports stay free. What you pay for is your own hardware — a tablet, a printer. Any paid extras added in the future will be optional and clearly marked; the core POS stays free.
pos.q10: Are there hidden fees or a commission?
pos.a10: No. No setup fee, no per-terminal fee, no per-user fee, and no commission on orders taken at the counter, at the table or from your online page.
pos.q11: Does the free POS run on an old Android tablet or iPad?
pos.a11: Yes. The main till runs in any modern browser, and there is a light tablet screen built for old devices — plain HTML that works on Android 4 tablets and early iPads — with sign-in, the menu with photos, notes, customers and open invoices.
pos.q12: Do I need an internet connection?
pos.a12: Yes — the POS is a web application, so the till, the kitchen screen and the online menu share one live menu over the internet. Ordinary 4G or Wi-Fi is enough; the pages are small and open in about a second.

pos.bandBody: Open the account now, add your menu today and take the first order tonight. No card, no contract, no monthly fee.
pos.a13: Yes. The whole platform — the POS, the kitchen display, the customer site, the admin panel and the API — is published on GitHub at github.com/majidtek/OrderOrange. You can read the code, report issues, contribute, or host it yourself.
